chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abdullah ibn Yaqoub, from Abdullah ibn Hilal who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered me to buy him an izar (lower garment). So I said to him, 'I could not find except for the extensive ones.' He said: 'Cut off from it and hem it.' He (the narrator) said, 'Then he said: My father said: And whatever exceeds the two heels, so it is in the Fire.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub – similar to it.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِزَاراً: A lower garment or loincloth worn by men

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the length of men's lower garments in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific boundary for men's lower garments, with Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructing Abdullah ibn Hilal to cut the excess fabric if it was too wide, reinforcing the prohibition of 'isbal' (letting garments hang below the ankles). The narration links this physical act of modesty to the spiritual danger of arrogance (kibr), as the Prophet (peace be upon him) declared that anything extending beyond the two heels is destined for the Fire, a ruling widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence as a sign of divine punishment for pride.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abdullah Bin Yaqoub, from Abdullah Bin Hilal who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> ordered me that I should buy a trouser for him<sup>asws</sup>. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I could not find except for the extensive ones’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Cut off from it and hem it’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And whatever exceeds the two heels, so it is in the Fire’.
Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from yunus Bin Yaqoub – similar to it’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ya‘qub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Hilal who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once commanded me to buy a loincloth for him. I said that I could only find wide ones. He (the Imam) said, ‘You must cut it and stitch its borders.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘My father has said, “Whatever of loincloth passes down the ankles is in the fire.’”
Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub a similar Hadith.
